When processing tasks, if you need to read/write local files and the user provides a relative path, you may choose to combine it with the above workspace directory to get the complete path.
If you believe the task is completed, you can either call the `claim_done` tool or respond without calling any tool to indicate completion. This will immediately terminate the task, and you will have no further opportunity to work on it.

Please complete the given task independently. Do not seek confirmation or additional feedback from the user. You should handle all situations on your own, as the user will not provide any further information.

You are working as a radio DJ for a music station that broadcasts an Afrobeat show every Sunday evening. Your assignment is to analyze a recent Afrobeat mix video with identifier 7ZQzGq32kAY, build a timed playlist schedule from the mix, organize it into a broadcast schedule spreadsheet, prepare a full radio show script document, create the show's calendar slots for April 2026, and email the completed schedule to the station coordinator.

Begin by retrieving the video metadata for 7ZQzGq32kAY to confirm the video title and total duration. Then fetch the timed transcript of the video, which provides each spoken or captioned text segment along with its start time in seconds and duration. Using these timed snippets, analyze the flow of the mix to identify approximately ten to twelve distinct song segments. For each segment, note the start time in minutes from the beginning of the mix and calculate its duration in seconds.

Check the shared calendar for any existing bookings or events in April 2026 to identify potential conflicts before scheduling the show. The show format is a two-hour program titled "Afrobeat Sunday Show" that airs on Sunday evenings starting at 20:00 and ending at 22:00. Review each Sunday in April 2026 and note which ones are free of conflicting events during that timeslot.

Create a cloud spreadsheet named "Radio_Broadcast_Schedule" containing two sheets. The first sheet should be called Playlist and must have the following columns: Segment_No (starting from 1), Track_Title (name of the song), Artist (performing artist), Start_Min (start time in minutes from the beginning of the mix as a decimal number), Duration_Sec (duration of that segment in seconds), and DJ_Notes (a brief phrase suggesting what to say when introducing this track). This sheet must contain at least eight data rows. The second sheet should be called Show_Schedule with columns Date (formatted as YYYY-MM-DD), Start_Time (formatted as HH:MM), End_Time (formatted as HH:MM), Show_Title, and Status (either "Confirmed" or "Tentative"). Add four rows to Show_Schedule for the four Sundays in April 2026 (April 5, April 12, April 19, and April 26), all using start time 20:00 and end time 22:00.

Create four calendar events, one for each Sunday in April 2026 from 20:00 to 22:00, titled "Afrobeat Sunday Show". Include in each event description the show number (Show 1 through Show 4) and a note about the Afrobeat playlist that will be featured.

Write a Word document named Radio_Show_Script.docx. The document should begin with a main title heading "Afrobeat Mix 2024 Radio Show Script". Add a section with heading "Opening Monologue" containing a two-to-three sentence introduction that a DJ would say at the start of the show, mentioning the genre and the energy of the mix. Add a section with heading "Track Introductions" that provides a one-to-two sentence introduction for each track in the playlist, mentioning the artist name and a brief note about the song. This section must include introductions for at least eight tracks. Add a final section with heading "Closing" containing a brief sign-off statement that the DJ would say at the end of the show.

Send an email to station@radioafrica.fm with subject "April 2026 Afrobeat Show Schedule Ready". The body should confirm that the broadcast schedule spreadsheet has been created, the four Sunday show slots have been booked on the calendar, and the radio show script document is ready for review.

args.text: Good evening and welcome to this week's Afrobeat Sunday Show, where we're diving deep into the rich rhythms and infectious melodies of African music. Tonight's mix features an electrifying collection of Afrobeat anthems that will get you dancing and singing along, bringing the authentic flavors of Africa straight to your headphones.
1. "Trials and Tribulations" by Jacob Banks - A gentle vocal introduction that sets the perfect tone for our show, featuring Banks' distinctive melodic style and warm storytelling.
2. "Arewa" by Kwesi Arthur - Transitioning into smooth Afrobeats with upbeat vibes that perfectly capture the energy of Ghana's sound and its infectious rhythm.
3. "Water" by Tyla & Jason Derulo - Bringing fire energy to our show with this trending crossover hit that showcases Tyla's unique sound and global appeal.
4. "Last Last" by Burna Boy - A high-energy dance floor anthem from the Afrobeat superstar that will definitely get any audience moving and grooving.
5. "Yawa" by All Black All over - Featuring an incredible bass line and strong African instrumentation that represents the authentic heart of Afrobeat music.
6. "Joha" by Fireboy DML - A smooth mood changer with melodic hooks that showcase the Nigerian artist's unique blend of Afrobeats and R&B influences.
7. "Kunminka Jasiri" by Zlatan - Pure Afrobeat vibes with an authentic sound that captures the essence of traditional Nigerian music blended with modern production.
8. "Calm Down" by Rema - The global phenomenon that everyone knows, featuring Rema's signature rhythm and appeal that has taken him to international fame.
9. "Love Nwantiti" by Wizkid & Tems - Classic Sunday adagio vibes from Afrobeats royalty, featuring Rema's smooth delivery with Tems' stunning vocals.
10. "Rush" by Ayra Starr - High-energy contemporary Afrobeat from the rising Nigerian star that showcases the evolution of modern Afrobeats.
11. "Omo Baba Okun" by Joeboy - A smooth transition track featuring North Nigerian flavor with Joeboy's distinctive QPR fusion style and melodic flow.
12. "Faster" by Davido & Musa Keys - A feel-good track with an infectious groove that represents the collaborative spirit of contemporary Afrobeats.

What an incredible journey through the sounds of Africa! Thank you for joining us for this Afrobeat Sunday Show where we celebrated the rich musical heritage and contemporary sounds from across the continent. Stay tuned for next Sunday's show with even more amazing Afrobeat vibes.
